title: Finding
description: One security finding from any engine or scanner, in one form. `severity` says how bad the finding is if it is real; `evidence` says how far the proof went. A code finding must have evidence. The fingerprint is the identity of the finding across runs. It maps to and from a SARIF 2.1.0 result.

id.description: The identifier that the producer gave the finding in its run, for example `ST-001` or a row identifier. It is not stable across runs; `fingerprint` is.

description.description: The claim, the evidence and the conditions of the exploit, as text.

ruleId.description: The rule of the engine that produced the finding: a CWE identifier, a scanner rule or an advisory identifier.

relatedLocations.description: Other locations that the finding cites, with no role in the path.

path.description: The path from the source of the input to the sink, in order.

cwe.description: CWE identifiers, the most specific first.

advisories.description: The identifiers of the advisories that the finding matches, for example CVE, GHSA or OSV identifiers.

fixedVersions.description: The versions of `component` that fix the advisories.

properties.description: Fields of the producer that the contract does not define, for example a rank or a route. A reader must not need them to understand the finding.

findingKind.title: FindingKind
findingKind.description: `code`: a weakness in the source code. The other kinds are the deterministic scanner types.

fingerprint.title: Fingerprint
fingerprint.description: The identity of a finding across runs, under a named scheme. Two findings with the same scheme and value are the same finding. The scheme names the material and the method, so a comparison is valid only within one scheme. Known schemes: `sentrytowerFindingHash/v1` (the public CLI: the first 32 hex digits of SHA-256 over the file, the first CWE and the title words), `sentrytowerScannerFinding/v1` (the scanner service: 64 hex digits), `sarifResultHash/v1` (a SARIF result with no fingerprint: the hex SHA-256 of the rule, the path, the start line and the message, joined by `|`). A SARIF result keeps the name of its `partialFingerprints` entry as the scheme.

scheme.description: The name of the scheme. The schemes of National Compute end in a version, `/v<n>`; a scheme from a SARIF producer keeps the name that the producer gave.

engine.title: Engine
engine.description: The engine or scanner that produced the finding.

mode.description: The part of the engine that found it, for example `deep-check` or `single-agent`.

target.title: Target
target.description: What was scanned. `repository`: a tree, at `revision` when it is a Git commit. `diff`: the change from `base` to `revision`, which touches `changedFiles`. `oci_image`: an image at `digest`.

locator.description: The name of the target, for example `github:owner/name`, a folder name or an image reference.

commit.title: CommitId
commit.description: A Git commit identifier: SHA-1 (40 hex digits) or SHA-256 (64 hex digits).

location.title: Location
location.description: A region of one file. `path` is relative to the root of the target and uses `/` separators.

note.description: What this code does in the finding.

excerpt.description: A short excerpt of the code, so that a reader can judge the citation without the file.

pathStep.title: PathStep
pathStep.description: One step of the path from the source of the input to the sink.

check.title: Check
check.description: The one check that the owner of the code runs to settle the claim.

intent.description: One line about what the check proves.

command.description: The shell command or code, ready to run.

minutes.description: The estimated time to run the check.
